newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan allows labour insurance fund to buy shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan allows labour insurance fund to buy shares.

text.p: A cabinet panel on Friday approved a proposal to allow Taiwan's T$188 billion state labour insurance fund to invest up to 30 percent of its holdings in the island's stock market.
Premier Lien Chan, the cabinet chief, is expected to sign the reform, officials said.

"The cabinet has given its approval and the liberalisation, after final signature from the premier, will become effective in the next week," an official from the cabinet's Council for Labour Affairs told Reuters by telephone.
The fund is worth some T$188 billion, meaning that under the 30 percent limit about T$56.4 billion would be allowed to be invested in stocks, the official said.

The fund had not been allowed to invest in the stock market under policies designed to maintain control over government monetary flows in the interest of stability as Taiwan liberalises its financial markets.

Under the reform measure, the fund may not put more than three percent of the its total value into any single stock. The fund also may not own more than five percent of any one listed firm's net assets.
The Council of Labour Affairs, a cabinet-level agency, had proposed the liberalisation in May.
